newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Bank Leumi roadshow a success.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Bank Leumi roadshow a success.

text.p: The head of MI Holdings, the Israeli government agency charged with selling state-owned banks, said on Sunday a European road-show to woo investors for a share offering of Bank Leumi was successful.
"The road-show was successful and the offering is proceeding as planned," MI Holdings managing director Meir Jacobsen told Reuters.

Jacobsen declined comment on a report in Israel's Haaretz newspaper that MI Holdings would sell more than a planned 10 percent of Leumi in light of the interest shown by European institutional investors in the bank, Israel's second largest.
"Nothing is closed yet. The extent and conditions of the offering will be announced on Monday afternoon," Jacobsen said.
He said that foreign investors could purchase some 70 percent of the shares offered. The government owns 82 percent of Leumi shares with the remainder already in the public domain.
Jacobsen said a prospectus for the sale would be published towards the end of the week and that the offering could go ahead next week.
Israel's parliament finance committee 10 days ago approved the sale of up to 20 percent of Bank Leumi, removing the last governmental hurdle to the offering.
Merrill Lynch and Lehman Brothers are the international distributors for the offering which will include shares and warrants.
The government expects to raise three billion shekels from the sale of Israeli bank shares this year.
